agree.reason: The reasons are concrete, and the partners' own change is persuasive, but a remote hire who lives 90 minutes away is told only that the firm 'isn't taking it lightly', with no commuting help or review offered, so the people most likely to leave have little reason to stay.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief and the causal claim about junior staff is hedged with 'we think', though 'until the end of 2027' assumes the year and 'we'll talk with each of you individually' is a commitment the brief doesn't give.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are repeated rather than worked: it never notes that 15 of 46 is a third of the firm, never turns the 30% into time lost per person, and leaves out the fact that 5 of 6 project leads already come in three days a week.

right_comparison.reason: It shows what has already happened (lost bids, slower development) but never says what continuing fully remote would lead to, or whether these problems are getting worse.

qualification.reason: A permanent change for people hired on remote terms needs a checkable condition, and the six-month review with staff would have supplied one with a date and a consequence, but it is left out.

objections.reason: It names the remote hires' grievance but answers it with sympathy only, leaving out the $150 commuting support and the desks arriving in August, and it never says plainly that there are no exceptions beyond the four, which invites individual requests.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured one-page email ahead of Friday's meeting, but it leaves out the 10 a.m. time, the main studio location and the HR contact, and is signed with placeholders instead of the partners' names.
